description: Lossless bounded block. Decode every {$ref:N} from shared_values[N] (fully expanded, one lookup). quote_span_table rows: [start,end,original_quote_type,original_quote_metadata]. Each SAME-entry attached_verbatim_passage_spans_ids and answer_quotation_spans_ids references table rows in order; exact quote is full supplied summary[start:end], Unicode half-open. Original object/string metadata retained; __transport_text_field__ names text/verbatim field, remove it on restoration. Span sha256_utf8 reconstructs as SHA256 of exact quote. answer_transport joins restored answer_quotations. All original raw fields/quotes/numeric/case fields reconstruct exactly. No keys or answers outside this fixed block supplied. No cross-entry or cross-reader borrowing.

rubric.correct: Every actually requested fact correct, resolved and summary-supported; equivalent complete meaning accepted; no material contradiction.
rubric.partial: Missing/unresolved requested fact with no material contradiction.
rubric.incorrect: Any material contradiction, including volunteered contextual claims.

global_constraints: No borrowing a fact from another question or reader.
Do not require ancillary source-only facts or contextual key facts excluded here.
Named board order may convey an order without listing every suit.
A clear operational equivalent passes without parroting key wording.
Semantic relation must be present: one user is not once total; paid use is not necessarily user pays; global three Visions is not personal draws; one unmatched site card is not all unmatched.
Free Chronicle together with affirmative Exile-winner permission may convey normal-offer waiver.
This file does not certify source audit or silently fix a fixed expected answer.

questions.question: How can Citizenship be offered and accepted during play, and what may or must be exchanged?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Grand Scepter holder (not taken this turn) offers any Exile including self exactly one Reliquary relic plus optional binding exchange favor,secrets,banners,non-Reliquary relics. Accepted: flip Citizen, replace all board/map warbands purple as available with recipient choosing shortfall removals/replacements, discard revealed Vision, Usurper→Oathkeeper, end Act if own turn, refresh full. Exchange agreed items; Chancellor gains uncovered mandatory modifier. All Imperials rule purple sites. Reliquary relics inaccessible to Campaign/Recover, powers unusable, do not count goals.

required_facts.expected_fact: Grand Scepter holder, not on turn taken, offers any Exile including self.
Must promise exactly one Reliquary relic; optional binding exchanges of favor/secrets/banners/non-Reliquary relics.
Exchange promised items and Chancellor gains uncovered mandatory Reliquary modifier.
Acceptance flips Citizen and replaces own board/map warbands purple, recipient choosing shortfall removals/replacements.
Discard revealed Vision, Usurper flips Oathkeeper, end Act if own turn, refresh full Supply.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: All Imperials rule purple sites; Reliquary immunity, unusable powers and goal exclusion.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Background rules are not additional offer/acceptance/exchange steps.
Source-only option absent from fixed expected facts; not required as an exchange mechanism.

questions.semantic_notes: Preserves established seed requested scope; equivalent unambiguous meaning accepted, no cross-question borrowing.

questions.question: Describe the Chronicle’s new Oath choice, Citizenship turnover, and world-deck rebuilding, including why the top stack is not 14 cards.
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Vision-only winner uses matching Oath; other/multiple-method win chooses any different Oath. Exile winner flips all Citizens even boxed to Exile then may offer other Exiles except newly flipped; accepted map garrisons replaced one each by winner warband (ignore normal offer). Rebuild remaining denizens: ten+two random Visions=12 top, fifteen+three Visions=18 middle, remaining denizens bottom. Chronicle aid 12 denizens+2 is erroneous.

required_facts.expected_fact: Vision-only winner chooses matching Oath; other/multiple-method victory chooses a different Oath.
Exile winner flips all Citizens including boxed to Exile, then may offer other Exiles except just-flipped, not self, ignoring normal offer rules.
Acceptors flip Citizen; replace garrisons at their ruled sites with one winner-color warband per site.
Rebuild remaining denizens: top ten denizens plus two random Visions equals twelve; middle fifteen plus remaining three equals eighteen; remaining denizens bottom.
Chronicle aid twelve-denizens-plus-two is erroneous and would incorrectly make fourteen.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Exact prose identifying shuffle/pool provenance beyond remaining-denizen rebuild.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Required fixed scope is remaining-denizen stack composition and corrected aid; no additional ritual or wording requirement when no wrong pool is asserted.

questions.semantic_notes: Preserves established seed requested scope; equivalent unambiguous meaning accepted, no cross-question borrowing. Free Chronicle plus affirmative unconditional Exile-winner offer can equivalently convey normal-offer waiver; exact no-Scepter/no-relic keywords are not demanded.

questions.question: In later-game setup with five players, how much favor goes in each bank, what is on the banners, and what resources and warbands start on each kind of player board?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Four favor per suit bank (three with two–four players). People’s Favor normal with one favor, Darkest Secret one secret. Chancellor two favor,one secret,three purple board warbands; other players one favor,one secret,three board warbands (own color Exile,purple Citizen). All full Supply.

required_facts.expected_fact: Four favor per suit bank.
People’s Favor normal with one favor; Darkest Secret with one secret.
Chancellor: two favor, one secret, three purple board warbands.
Other players: one favor, one secret, three own-color Exile/purple Citizen board warbands.
All begin full Supply.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Three favor per bank with two–four players.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: The scenario has five players; other player-count setups are context.

questions.question: How is the Chronicled map dealt, where are starting Imperial garrisons placed, and which sites receive favor/secrets during later-game setup?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Deal saved sites/attached cards Cradle then Provinces then Hinterland top-down. Two purple at topmost faceup Cradle, one at each other faceup site with denizen or intact edifice; ruin alone insufficient. Put printed favor/secrets on prompted sites from bank; Chancellor allocates insufficient favor.

required_facts.expected_fact: Saved sites with attachments: Cradle, Provinces, Hinterland, each top-down.
Two purple at topmost faceup Cradle; one at each other faceup site with denizen/intact edifice; ruin alone does not qualify.
Apply printed prompts to applicable sites from shared bank; Chancellor allocates insufficient favor.

questions.question: May later-game players choose a Citizen board or any pawn location? Does starting Citizen receive a relic, and who starts with a banner/title?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Non-Chancellors choose in turn order among boards on saved sides, so Citizen only if saved Citizen. No starting relic for Citizen. Pawns any faceup site except Chancellor top Cradle. Chancellor Oathkeeper, gets Darkest Secret for Devotion or People’s Favor for People.

required_facts.expected_fact: Non-Chancellors choose boards on saved sides, so Citizen only if saved Citizen.
Any faceup site except Chancellor must top faceup Cradle.
No starting relic for Citizen.
Chancellor is Oathkeeper and additionally gets Darkest Secret for Devotion or People’s Favor for People.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Board selection is in turn order.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Permission to choose saved Citizen status is asked, not selection priority among players.

questions.question: Describe later-game discard seeding, starting adviser selection and Vision counting. Are starting Reliquary relic placements chosen or random?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Seed each discard with one of three total bottom-world-deck cards; each player draws three bottom cards, then turn order chooses facedown adviser and discards other two using pawn region after placing pawn. Advance Visions Drawn for drawn Visions. Four Reliquary relics randomly one per space.

required_facts.expected_fact: Three total bottom-world cards, one per regional discard.
Each player draws three bottom cards; in turn order place pawn, keep one facedown adviser, discard other two by pawn-region rules.
Advance Visions Drawn for Visions drawn.
Four relics random, one per Reliquary space.

questions.question: In first-game packet setup, which sites/pawns/garrisons/denizens/advisers are faceup or facedown, and where is Ivory Eye?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Faceup Plains top Cradle,purple pawn,two purple garrison,faceup Longbows; faceup Mountain top Provinces,Red/Blue pawns,one purple,faceup Taming Charm; faceup Rocky Coast top Hinterland,Yellow pawn,one purple,faceup Elders. Other sites facedown. Facedown advisers Chancellor Forest Paths,Red Animal Playmates,Blue Naysayers,Yellow A Small Favor. Ivory Eye facedown at Mountain. Preserve packet deck order.
questions.source_references: Playbook pp6–7; original Playbook pp6–7 setup diagrams, fresh source-key-clarification-09

required_facts.expected_fact: Top Cradle faceup Plains: purple pawn, two purple, faceup Longbows.
Top Provinces faceup Mountain: Red/Blue pawns, one purple, faceup Taming Charm.
Top Hinterland faceup Rocky Coast: Yellow pawn, one purple, faceup Elders; other sites facedown.
Chancellor Forest Paths; Red Animal Playmates; Blue Naysayers; Yellow A Small Favor.
Facedown at Mountain.

contextual_exclusions.rationale: This question asks placements and faceup/facedown state, not deck preparation (asked separately in Q084).

questions.question: Can you act at a remote ruled site to Muster/Trade, use a normal Action power there, or use a battle plan at your pawn site that you do not rule? How do persistent powers differ?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Muster/Trade only pawn site. Normal card power accessible by ruling card or pawn at its site, so remote ruled Action accessible. Battle plan requires rule, pawn alone insufficient. Persistent black-thick-braid power affects specified players ignoring ordinary access.

required_facts.expected_fact: Only at pawn site, so remote rule is insufficient.
Ruling the card grants access remotely; pawn at its site also grants ordinary access.
Battle plan requires rule; pawn presence alone is insufficient.
Persistent power affects its specified players regardless of ordinary access.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Thick black braid identifies persistent power.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Visual identifier is context; the requested distinction is operation/access.

questions.question: A defensive battle plan costs favor and a secret. Where do those go when used outside your turn, when is the secret ready again, and can that plan already hold resources?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Favor immediately matching bank,secret stays own board facedown,cannot place/burn facedown to pay; ready at own Rest. Battle-plan payment allowed on occupied card once per Campaign. Does not allow Muster/Trade on occupied card.

required_facts.expected_fact: Favor immediately to matching bank; secret stays own board facedown.
Cannot pay with that facedown secret until readied; own Rest flips it up.
Battle-plan payment may use a card already holding resources.

contextual_exclusions.rationale: General use limit is not independently asked by this narrow payment/occupancy question.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Muster/Trade still cannot use occupied card.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Other major-action eligibility is outside the asked defensive-plan payment.

questions.question: When are ordinary action modifiers used, may the same modifier apply twice to one action or to later actions, and may an active modifier be discarded?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: At modified action start,in any order; each once per action, only current action. No-cost modifier can modify multiple different actions. Usually optional except must/cannot; cannot discard while modifying current action.

required_facts.expected_fact: At modified action start, any chosen order, affecting current action.
Each modifier once per action; no-cost modifier may apply to later distinct actions.
Cannot discard while it modifies the current action.

contextual_exclusions.rationale: Whether to decline a modifier is not separately asked; timing/repetition/active discard are.

questions.question: What is the timing order for When Played powers, how often may Wake/Rest powers happen, and may a paid power be used if it will have no effect?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: When Played mandatory after playing faceup,after site-favor gain,Homeland effects and modifiers. Wake once each in Wake; Rest optional once each at end Rest. May pay/use even zero effect,resolve as much as possible except may parts.

required_facts.expected_fact: Mandatory on faceup play after site-play favor, Homeland effects and modifiers.
Wake powers once each in Wake; Rest powers optional once each at end Rest.
May pay/use even when effect will do nothing.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Resolve as much as possible except explicit may parts.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: General resolution rule is context, not an additional requested no-effect-use condition; any contrary volunteered ruling is still wrong.

questions.question: What do tree, person and chain restrictions do to faceup play/move/swap/discard, and how are two adviser-limit reductions combined and checked when played?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Tree site-only,person adviser-only,also move/swap; locked cannot discard/move/swap once played except Chronicle. Restriction banners on facedown cards do not apply. Use lowest changed adviser limit,not additive; discard to satisfy new limit before playing card,not old limit. Locked cards remain protected.

required_facts.expected_fact: Tree site-only; person adviser-only, including moving/swapping.
Locked faceup cards cannot discard/move/swap except Chronicle.
Lowest applicable limit, not additive; satisfy new limit by discarding before playing incoming card, respecting locks.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Facedown restriction banners do not apply.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Question explicitly frames faceup restrictions; facedown exception is context.

questions.question: Who can play Conspiracy, what exact theft conditions/cost apply, can two advisers match one enemy adviser, and where does Conspiracy end?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Anyone, even Imperials. Burn one secret to take one relic or banner from any player whose pawn is at your site. Two of your own faceup advisers must each match the suit of at least one of that target player’s advisers; both may match the same adviser. The target need not be an enemy. Playing Conspiracy does not replace a revealed true Vision; banner seizure applies; Conspiracy goes to the box even if no theft is made.

required_facts.expected_fact: Anyone, including Imperials.
Burn one secret to take one relic/banner from any co-located player; target need not be enemy.
Two own faceup advisers each match at least one target adviser; both may match same adviser.
Banner theft invokes seizure penalty.
Return to box even if no theft made.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Does not replace an existing true Vision.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: True-Vision replacement is not asked here; no contradictory slot ruling is permitted.

questions.question: May you freely discard a faceup adviser, move warbands onto an empty site, or pick up the last site warband? What changes with Citizens and co-located Imperial pawns?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: No voluntary faceup discard unless rule prompts; no ordinary drop on empty bandit site; pick up all but last own site warband. Drop only at ruled pawn site. Citizen pickup requires Chancellor permission. Imperial pawns co-located can give/take board warbands with other player permission. Bandit Crown permits last physical pickup.

required_facts.expected_fact: No, only when a rule permits/requires.
Ordinary drop only at ruled pawn site, not an empty bandit site.
May pick up all but last own site warband; Bandit Crown permits last physical pickup.
Citizen pickup needs Chancellor permission.
Co-located Imperial pawns may give/take board warbands with other player’s permission.

questions.question: What relics can you peek at without paying Supply, and may a relic peeked at earlier be inspected again after moving away?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Any facedown relic at own pawn site; any previously peeked specific relic again from any site. Scepter holder can peek Reliquary (subject cannot use Scepter taken this turn). Other sites’ unpeeked relics require power.

required_facts.expected_fact: Facedown relic at own pawn site; previously peeked specific relic again from anywhere.
Grand Scepter holder may peek Reliquary, subject to no powers on turn taken.
Previously peeked specific relic remains inspectable remotely.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Other unpeeked remote relics require an applicable power.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Consequence of the eligibility list; no separate generic exception phrase is required.

questions.question: If the Scepter holder exiles a Citizen, how is favor payment calculated, which warbands change color, and does this end the recipient’s Act?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Pay five,+one for Citizen Oathkeeper,+one Citizen People’s Favor,minus one payer Oathkeeper,minus one payer People’s Favor. Flip Exile,replace board purple with own color,refresh full; map garrisons stay purple. Does not by itself end recipient Act.

required_facts.expected_fact: Five favor, +1 each for recipient Oathkeeper/People’s Favor, −1 each for payer Oathkeeper/People’s Favor.
Only recipient’s board purple changes to own color; map garrisons stay purple.
Does not by itself end recipient Act.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Flip board Exile and refresh full Supply.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Status label is inherent in exiling; full Supply is another consequence not asked by payment/colors/Act clauses.

questions.question: How is self-exile paid, who is prohibited from doing it, what warbands change, and does Act continue?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Citizen gives Scepter holder favor equal board warbands plus secrets on own board and denizen/relic/edifice cards. Scepter holder cannot self-exile. Flip Exile,replace board purple with own color,full Supply,end Act. Map purple stays.

required_facts.expected_fact: Citizen gives Scepter holder favor equal own board warbands plus own secrets on board and denizen/relic/edifice cards.
A Citizen holding the Scepter cannot self-exile.
Only board purple becomes own color; map purple stays.
End Act.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Refresh full Supply and explicit board flip.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Refresh not asked; status change is inherent in self-exile, not a separate wording demand.

questions.question: Two players tie the current title holder; later the holder falls behind two tied leaders. Who holds title, and when is Supremacy transferred during Campaign?
questions.fixed_expected_answer: Current holder keeps when tied for goal. If holder no longer meets goal,chooses among tied qualifying others. New recipient Oathkeeper-side. Supremacy transfer after Campaign ends,not temporary mid-Campaign losses. Empire collective purple rule credits Chancellor.

required_facts.expected_fact: Holder keeps title while tied for goal.
Outgoing holder chooses among qualifying tied leaders; recipient receives Oathkeeper side.
Transfer at Campaign end, not temporary mid-Campaign rule losses.

contextual_exclusions.key_or_source_fact: Empire collective purple-site rule credits Chancellor.
contextual_exclusions.rationale: Question does not introduce Imperial collective holdings; this is background Supremacy context.
